audit_findings.title: Negative OE is being grown in the wrong economic direction
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $701.0 million operating-PV and $11.25 per-share spread between BULL and BEAR; filed 2025 Company-funded capex was $488.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The negative OE anchor is multiplied by positive growth, while the maintenance-versus-growth capex classification determines the anchor itself.
audit_findings.evidence: Utility plant expenditures in 2025 were $517.0 million, including Company-funded of $488.4 million and developer-funded of $28.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The scenario inversion is demonstrated: increasing growth from negative 2% to positive 5% makes operating PV fall from negative $1.478 billion to negative $2.179 billion, causing the stated BULL case to be worth less than BEAR. Whether the $488.4 million Company-funded expenditure was properly normalized to maintenance capex is unresolved, but its scale relative to the negative $138.9 million anchor makes the issue reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify negative-anchor sign handling; reconstruct 2025 OE using identified maintenance capex, developer funding, and rate-recovery timing; then rerun all scenarios with economically ordered assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter omits the announced Nexus acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: filed approximately $218.0 million purchase price, $109.0 million combined rate base, and 36,000 equivalent residential connections; separate BVRT purchase price $45.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes forecast OE, growth, acquisition cash outflow, debt, future shares, and the ownership perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: In February of 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to purchase Nexus Water Group’s Nevada and Oregon water and wastewater systems (the Systems) for approximately $ 218.0 million, subject to the finalization of closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated because the transaction had been announced, board-approved, and submitted for regulatory approval before the valuation date, while the model records a null perimeter. Closing remained conditional in the latest filing, and the acquired earnings and financing mix are unquantified. Nevertheless, a $218.0 million transaction requiring cash, debt, and equity financing is reasonably capable of changing the modeled ownership claim and valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain transaction status as of September 6, 2026 and build closed, failed, and probability-weighted pro forma cases incorporating acquired OE, capital needs, purchase consideration, debt, and issued shares; separately incorporate the $45.0 million BVRT transaction.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling omits structurally expected equity issuance
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $253.4 million remaining ATM capacity; computed approximately 5.065 million shares at $50.03, equal to 8.1% of the modeled 62.305457 million shares; actual future issuance unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future equity financing increases the per-share denominator while financing capital projects and acquisitions included in future operations.
audit_findings.evidence: In future periods, the Company intends to issue common stock and long-term debt to finance operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The company issued 2.106557 million ATM shares during the first half of 2026 and explicitly intends further balanced debt-and-equity financing. The modeled fully diluted count exceeds the July outstanding count by only about 0.466 million shares and therefore does not cover the remaining ATM capacity. Actual issuance price, timing, and the incremental OE earned on funded investments are unresolved, so the record cannot establish the net materiality.
audit_findings.action: Forecast shares issued for the capital program, Nexus financing, and remaining ATM usage; link each issuance to the associated investment and OE, and rerun value per share using annual diluted share counts.

audit_findings.title: Refundable developer advances may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $210.638 million liability, $10.459 million due in 2026, and $9.462 million refunded in 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Developer refunds are financing cash outflows that must either reduce forecast OE or be represented by an equivalent deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Advances of $ 210.6 million and $ 202.6 million, at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, will be refunded primarily over a 40-year period from the date the advance was received in equal annual amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual obligation and its scale are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show the detailed OE construction needed to establish whether refunds were already captured consistently. The 2026 refund equals 7.5% of the absolute $138.9 million OE anchor, while the total liability equals 11.0% of the absolute $1.908 billion base equity value, so omission may affect value but materiality cannot be established without tracing the associated developer-funded assets and receipts.
audit_findings.action: Trace advance receipts, developer-funded capex, and refunds through each historical OE year and forecast; if refunds are absent, rerun with the filed payment schedule or deduct an equivalent liability without double counting.

audit_findings.title: PFAS proceeds may have been treated as shareholder cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum bridge exposure $43.445 million, computed $0.70 per share; filed first-half 2026 PFAS receipts were $18.471 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer-benefit PFAS funds could improperly enter value through the cash bridge or, if misclassified, OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is required by the Commissions to provide the benefit of the PFAS settlement proceeds to customers through CIAC once PFAS related remediation projects are placed in service.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that PFAS proceeds are financing cash flows and regulatory liabilities rather than shareholder earnings. Even if the entire $43.445 million cash bridge were unavailable to shareholders, the effect is only about $0.70 per share, versus the $80.66 per-share gap between the $50.03 market price and negative $30.63 base value. It therefore cannot change the stated valuation conclusion, although the bridge classification should still be corrected if reconciliation shows PFAS cash is included.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 cash balance to PFAS regulatory liabilities and settlement receipts, exclude any customer-benefit amount from excess cash, and confirm that no PFAS receipt entered OE.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 numerator includes a lease expiring before the valuation date
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $13.0 million of 2025 Hawthorne revenue, computed as 1.3% of $1.00014 billion consolidated operating revenue; OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration removes Hawthorne revenue, operating costs, and capital requirements from normalized OE and may create a separate nonrecurring reimbursement.
audit_findings.evidence: The City of Hawthorne capital lease is a 15-year lease and expires in August of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes an August 2026 contractual expiration and states that renewal was not expected, although the supplied record does not confirm the post-expiration outcome. The gross revenue at risk was only 1.3% of consolidated 2025 operating revenue, and its net OE contribution must be smaller after operating costs and capital requirements. That scale is not reasonably capable of closing the valuation's $80.66 per-share base-case shortfall or reversing its negative conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the actual expiration, remove Hawthorne's recurring revenue, costs, and capital requirements from normalized OE, and recognize any reimbursement of unamortized improvements separately as nonrecurring value.
